title: 2022 AMC 12B Problem 19
statement: In \(\triangle ABC\) medians \(\overline{AD}\) and \(\overline{BE}\) intersect at \(G\) and \(\triangle AGE\) is equilateral. Then \(\cos(C)\) can be written as \(\dfrac{m\sqrt p}{n},\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are relatively prime positive integers and \(p\) is a positive integer not divisible by the square of any prime. What is \(m + n + p?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(a = BC,\) \(b = CA,\) \(c = AB.\) Since \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AC,\) \(AE = \tfrac{b}{2}.\) The centroid gives \(AG = \tfrac23 m_a\) and \(GE = \tfrac13 m_b,\) where \(m_a, m_b\) are the medians from \(A\) and \(B.\)

Equilateral \(\triangle AGE\) means \(AG = GE = AE.\) From \(\tfrac23 m_a = \tfrac{b}{2}\) we get \(m_a = \tfrac34 b,\) which with \(m_a^2 = \tfrac{2b^2 + 2c^2 - a^2}{4}\) gives \(2c^2 - a^2 = \tfrac{b^2}{4}.\) From \(\tfrac13 m_b = \tfrac{b}{2}\) we get \(m_b = \tfrac32 b,\) giving \(a^2 + c^2 = 5b^2.\)

Solving, \(c^2 = \tfrac{7b^2}{4}\) and \(a^2 = \tfrac{13b^2}{4}.\) Taking \(b = 2\) gives \(a^2 = 13,\) \(c^2 = 7,\) so \[ \begin{aligned} \cos C &= \dfrac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} \\ &= \dfrac{13 + 4 - 7}{2 \cdot \sqrt{13} \cdot 2} \\ &= \dfrac{5\sqrt{13}}{26}. \end{aligned} \]

Then \(m + n + p = 5 + 26 + 13 = 44.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The centroid splits \(AD\) so \(AG = \tfrac23 AD,\) and \(GE = \tfrac13 BE;\) also \(AE = \tfrac12 AC\)
Set all three equal and use the median-length formula to relate the sides, then apply the law of cosines
